steps.title: Comparatives and superlatives
steps.html:
AdjectiveComparativeSuperlative
short: quietquieter thanthe quietest
ending in -y: lazylazier thanthe laziest
long: creativemore creative thanthe most creative
goodbetter thanthe best
badworse thanthe worst
farfurther thanthe furthest
the sameas useful as—

One-syllable adjectives add -er / -est: quiet → quieter → the quietest. Double a final consonant after one vowel: big → bigger.

Adjectives of two or more syllables use more / the most: more careful, the most creative. Two-syllable words ending in -y take -ier: lazy → lazier.

than after a comparative; the before a superlative. She is quieter than me. He is the most useful person here.

Make the difference bigger or smaller with much or a bit: much quieter, a bit more careful.

You compared amounts in Lesson 14 (more than my electricity bill). This lesson compares qualities.

steps.title: The quiet ones
steps.html:
Why the loudest person is not always the right one.

Reading

In most offices the loudest person in the room gets the work. That is not the same thing as the best person for it.

Susan Cain’s best-selling book Quiet made a simple point: about a third of us are introverts, and almost every school and workplace is built for the other two thirds. Open-plan offices are noisier than they were. Meetings reward the person who speaks first, not the person who thinks longest.

An introvert is not a shy person. Shyness is fear of other people; being an introvert is about energy. Extroverts get energy from a room full of people. Introverts spend it there, and get it back alone. An introvert can be very confident and very sociable — just not for eight hours at a time.

Cain’s argument is not that introverts are better. It is that the two are as useful as each other, and that we only listen to one of them. The most creative ideas in her research often came from people who were quieter in the meeting and more careful in what they said. They were also the hardest people to hear.

Her advice to companies is simple and cheap: give people a place to work alone, and send the questions out before the meeting, not during it. The most useful person in your team may be the one who has not spoken yet.

steps.title: Choose the best answer.
options: Introverts and extroverts are equally useful, but we only listen to one of them.
Introverts are better workers than extroverts in almost every job.
Open-plan offices should be closed and replaced with small rooms.
steps.answer: Introverts and extroverts are equally useful, but we only listen to one of them.
steps.why: “It is that the two are as useful as each other, and that we only listen to one of them.”
